evals.prompt: Prepare a sprint review for the team and the Product Manager based on the issues completed in the last sprint. I want a value-oriented narrative and a presenter recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Includes factual context, main message, value blocks, deliveries table and an indication of who presents each block.
expectations: Clearly identifies the interval and the analysis mode (Scrum)
Groups deliveries by perceived value and not just as a list of issues
Suggests presenters based on the assignees and their real contribution
Focuses on the impact for the business, the user or the operation
Excludes non-deliverable items, such as test or quality artifacts

evals.prompt: Create a product demo for stakeholders based on what was delivered this week and indicate what needs alignment to decide the next step.
evals.expected_output: Presents a short, impact-oriented narrative with a well-defined script and next steps.
expectations: Resolves the mode as Kanban or time window and asks for clarification if necessary
Uses a simple structure of context, delivery, impact and decision
Avoids technical excess with no link to value
Clearly flags who can present each block
If data is missing, states the absence of evidence instead of inferring impact

evals.prompt: I want a product review with a business audience. Gather only what was completed and deliver a main message, risks and the ideal session format.
evals.expected_output: Provides an executive briefing focused on decision and perceived value.
expectations: Keeps factual and professional language
Does not invent business impact without evidence
Includes dependencies, risks and follow-up questions
Suggests the appropriate format based on the audience and the session context

evals.prompt: I want today's demo; prepare the briefing based on what was delivered. Don't tell me whether it is Scrum or Kanban; just do the summary.
evals.expected_output: Asks for clarification about the analysis context before continuing, because the request is ambiguous between sprint and time window.
expectations: Recognizes the ambiguity between Sprint and Kanban
Asks the user to confirm the analysis type before proceeding
Does not automatically assume it is Scrum or Kanban
Keeps the answer short, focused on clarification and without inventing data

evals.prompt: Prepare the sprint review of the Checkout team for the Product Manager and the team. I want the summary to highlight perceived value, dependencies and who explains each block.
evals.expected_output: Delivers a briefing with factual context, main message, value blocks, presentation by impact and owners per theme.
expectations: Recognizes that this is a Scrum/sprint context
Groups deliveries by value and not just by ticket
Identifies main owners and proposes presenters
Includes relevant dependencies or risks
Focuses on the value for the business, the user or the operation

evals.prompt: I want a product demo for the interested parties, focused on impact, ordering by relevance and recommendations on who presents each theme.
evals.expected_output: Creates a short, executive narrative with presentation order, value and session briefing.
expectations: Resolves the Kanban/time window mode when the question mentions interested parties and a period
Orders the presentation by impact and not by Jira chronology
Presents a clear main message
Suggests the role of each presenter
Keeps factual language that is useful for the audience

evals.prompt: Prepare the sprint review for leadership. I want only what was completed, the main message and the points of attention before the meeting takes place.
evals.expected_output: Summarizes the deliverables, the perceived value and the risks or decisions that deserve attention.
expectations: Includes factual context and the review period
Considers only completed and deliverable items
Does not invent business metrics without evidence
Includes risks, dependencies and follow-up
Keeps the language oriented to the executive decision

evals.prompt: I want an internal team demo to align on what was delivered in the last week. I'm not interested in a very long technical report, but a value narrative with an indication of who shows what.
evals.expected_output: Presents a short, practical view with a briefing, value blocks and presentation per subject.
expectations: Identifies the time window and the Kanban context
Groups deliveries by value theme
Reduces technical detail when it adds no value to the session
Defines who presents each block
Keeps the focus on what changed and why it matters

evals.prompt: Do a product review with a cross-functional audience. I'd like to prioritize the completed deliveries, explain the perceived impact and indicate who should speak about each part.
evals.expected_output: Creates a briefing with goals, value blocks, risks and a logical presentation order for the meeting.
expectations: Uses a clear structure of context, value and decision
Distinguishes between team, stakeholders and cross-functional audience
Suggests who presents based on experience and real responsibility
Includes dependencies and follow-up questions
Avoids impact inferences that have no support

evals.prompt: Prepare next week's demo for the internal customer. I want a view of the impact, a simple narrative and a team recommendation for the main blocks.
evals.expected_output: Produces a briefing focused on the value for the internal customer, what changed and who presents each part.
expectations: Resolves the audience target and adapts the level of detail
Keeps the session oriented to value and decision
Suggests presenters appropriately for the context
Clearly distinguishes between delivery and message exaggeration
Does not include test or management items as a main delivery

evals.prompt: I want a sprint review with several small deliveries. Group them by benefit for users and business and make a presentation script focused on what leadership needs to know.
evals.expected_output: Offers a summary organized by themes, with perceived value and presentation sequence for the meeting.
expectations: Groups deliveries by theme instead of listing them individually
Keeps the focus on the value for the user and for the business
Suggests presentation order by relevance
Includes risks and next steps
Does not mix tests and management with value delivery

evals.prompt: Can you prepare the product demo based on the issues completed this fortnight? I want a strong main message, deadlines and a presenter recommendation for each block.
evals.expected_output: Produces an objective version for a business meeting, focused on impact and presentation by blocks.
expectations: Identifies the analysis as a time window or Kanban
Uses a short, executive structure
Includes a value summary and session goals
Suggests who presents based on real responsibility
Avoids claims without factual support

evals.prompt: I want the sprint review preparation for the team and the PO. Gather the completed deliveries, identify the value and tell me how to organize the presentation.
evals.expected_output: Generates a session-oriented briefing with narrative, value blocks, deliveries and responsibilities.
expectations: Recognizes the Scrum context
Relates each delivery to perceived value
Defines who should present each block
Includes a suggested script for the meeting
Keeps the language clear and without exaggeration

evals.prompt: Do a product demo for a business audience with little technical context. I want to show what changed, why it matters and what needs alignment.
evals.expected_output: Creates an executive briefing focused on the business impact, not on technical detail.
expectations: Adapts the level of detail to the audience
Reduces the weight of technical details when they are not relevant
Focuses on the business or user impact
Includes what needs alignment or decision
Avoids inventing results that do not exist

evals.prompt: Prepare the sprint review for the engineering team and the Scrum Master. I want a clear summary of the delivery and who best explains each part.
evals.expected_output: Delivers a technical, structured briefing with value themes, presenters and session script.
expectations: Respects the Scrum context and the sprint window
Uses a structure sufficient for the technical team
Assigns the presentation realistically to the developers
Includes risks, dependencies and follow-up
Does not mix support work with business value

evals.prompt: I want the preparation of a product review from deliveries completed in the last 30 days. Organize the deliveries by impact and help me decide what to show first.
evals.expected_output: Presents a briefing with temporal context, value blocks, presentation order and script recommendation.
expectations: Identifies the analysis as a time window or Kanban
Orders the presentation by impact
Suggests a main theme and value narrative
Includes owners for each block
Does not assume results without evidence

evals.prompt: I want a demo for leadership with limited time. Read through the completed deliveries and recommend only the blocks worth showing.
evals.expected_output: Delivers a short, prioritized, decision-oriented version, focused on the most relevant themes.
expectations: Prioritizes by value relevance and not by the number of deliveries
Pays attention to the meeting's available time
Includes only eligible and completed deliveries
Suggests order and main presenter
Keeps executive language

evals.prompt: Prepare a sprint review for the team and the internal customer, with a summary of what changed, why it matters and how to present without losing the focus on value.
evals.expected_output: Provides a session briefing with main message, value blocks and an indication of who presents each theme.
expectations: Recognizes the Scrum context and the need to narrate the value
Includes enough factual context for the meeting
Assigns presenters based on real contribution
Focuses on the value for the internal customer and for the team
Does not include items that do not represent a delivery

evals.prompt: I want a product demo for an alignment meeting with stakeholders and PMO. Make a clear summary of what was delivered, why this matters and what the risks and pending decisions are.
evals.expected_output: Creates an executive briefing, clear and ready for decision, focused on impact and risks.
expectations: Uses a structure suited to a decision-making audience
Includes risks, dependencies and pending decisions
Focuses on the perceived value and the impact for the organization
Suggests presenters relevant to the theme
Keeps the text factual and not dependent on inferences

evals.prompt: I want you to prepare a sprint review for the product team, without inventing metrics or impacts. Use only what is supported by the completed issues and show the best presentation order.
evals.expected_output: Produces a prudent, focused and factual briefing, with narrative, order and owners.
expectations: Recognizes that it must work only with evidence
Does not invent financial impact, ROI or adoption
Clearly explains the order by relevance
Includes risks and dependencies, if any
Uses safe and objective language

evals.prompt: Do a product review from the work completed in the last two cycles. I want the main message, value blocks, deliveries to present and presenter suggestions.
evals.expected_output: Generates a structured briefing, focused on perceived value and presentation by block.
expectations: Resolves whether the context is Scrum or time window before synthesizing
Groups deliveries by value and not by isolated area
Suggests presenters based on real responsibility
Includes risks and dependency control
Emphasizes what the audience needs to decide or align on

evals.prompt: I want an internal delivery demo for the team and the business leaders. Make a summary of the completed deliveries, how to communicate them and who can lead each theme.
evals.expected_output: Creates a presentation briefing with clear structure, prioritization and distribution of owners.
expectations: Adapts the level of detail to the audience
Excludes test or management items as a main delivery
Groups by value and by perceived impact
Includes presentation by theme and assignment of owners
Pays attention to the business context and the decision

evals.prompt: Prepare a sprint review for the team and the tech lead. I want a view of what was delivered and a recommendation on which part should be explained by whom.
evals.expected_output: Delivers a technical and practical briefing with value themes, risks and presentation owners.
expectations: Recognizes the session as Scrum/sprint
Distinguishes between delivery and technical risk
Assigns the implementation explanation to the appropriate owner
Includes dependencies and the necessary decision
Keeps the language oriented to facts and clarity

evals.prompt: I want the preparation of a product demo for stakeholders and for the team. Summarize the completed deliveries, the main message and who speaks in each part without creating excess technical detail.
evals.expected_output: Generates an executive briefing with a short narrative, focus on value and presenters defined by theme.
expectations: Identifies the Kanban/time window context
Adapts the content to the audience
Keeps the explanation of value and impact first
Suggests presenters realistically
Avoids impact inferences without evidence
